source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Require an exact eight-week taper for every long-term PPI user because any faster reduction produces permanent pathologic acid hypersecretion.","B":"Warn that transient rebound upper-GI symptoms may occur after long-term PPI discontinuation and that either tapering or abrupt stopping can be considered.","C":"Avoid abrupt discontinuation in every patient because rebound symptoms are uniformly dangerous and cannot be managed clinically.","D":"Continue the PPI indefinitely after one year of treatment even when the original indication has resolved and no maintenance indication remains."}}
source_row.rationale: AGA best-practice advice supports regular review of indication, warns about transient symptoms from rebound acid hypersecretion after long-term discontinuation, and states that dose tapering or abrupt discontinuation can be considered.

source_row.stem: A client has taken a proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) long term but no longer has a clear ongoing indication. Which deprescribing teaching is most accurate?
